        Idea:
Design a robust end-to-end live test harness for the Reigh platform that exercises the individual-user worker path (NOT the orchestrator-managed worker path) against a specific user identified by Reigh access [REDACTED] Two variants of one live test, both targeting a real RunPod GPU, both creating real spoof tasks in Supabase for that specific user, both waiting for actual task completion and verifying generations were produced end-to-end. Variant A 'Fresh Install': spin up a new RunPod pod using the orchestrator's create_pod_and_wait approach, SSH in and clone reigh-worker into a folder with a NEW name (NOT Reigh-Worker, e.g. Reigh-Worker-LiveTest), run buildWorkerLaunchLine-equivalent install/launch with [REDACTED] --wgp-profile 3 --idle-release-minutes 0, wait for heartbeat, insert spoof tasks in Supabase scoped to the user that the token resolves to (via user_api_tokens.jti_hash), poll until each task reaches Complete with generations row, report pass/fail per task with output URLs, terminate pod via terminate_pod() with opt-out flag. Variant B 'Update Existing': target an existing pod with /workspace/Reigh-Worker/ installed (or spawn+standard-install then take over), push current local working copy of reigh-worker/ to a temporary branch on banodoco/Reigh-Worker, SSH in, git fetch+checkout+pull, uv sync --locked, cleanly restart worker with --reigh-access-token for test user, run same task matrix, on success optionally delete temp branch and restore pod to previous branch/state. Variant B must not clobber pods doing real user work — include safety check for in-flight tasks. Task matrix (one of each): travel_orchestrator standard Wan 2 images 1 segment, travel_orchestrator LTX variant, individual_travel_segment single segment, qwen_image_style with style ref, qwen_image text-to-image, qwen_image_2512, qwen_image_edit, z_image_turbo I2I. Stages: (1) prep/finalize unknowns, (2) build shared primitives (token→user resolver, task spoofer, poll-until-complete, SSH helpers reused from orchestrator), (3) build Variant A driver, (4) build Variant B driver, (5) dry-run/smoke-test the harness itself, (6) first real run, (7) cleanup/documentation. For each stage: concrete deliverables, files to touch, risks, validation.

User notes and answers:
- User decisions on blockers and open questions (authoritative — supersedes earlier plan choices):

BLOCKER 1 (isolation): [REDACTED] is ALREADY a dedicated test user account. It has no production work and is explicitly a test token. User confirmed we can proceed using this token directly. Still do a defensive preflight check (abort if any unexpected non-test Queued/In-Progress task exists for the user, as a safety net), but no need to pause production, create a new test user, or use service-role for claims.

BLOCKER 2 (readiness signal): Option (a). Inject BOTH the PAT ([REDACTED]) AND SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY into the pod. The worker must still run the INDIVIDUAL-USER PAT path for task claims (WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker) — this is a hard requirement. The service role key is injected purely so heartbeat RPCs work and the standard ready_for_tasks detection path is available. Do NOT switch to service-role claim path.

BLOCKER 3 (Variant B takeover safety gate): Orchestrator's call — use option (a). Implement a PAT-aware in-flight check that queries tasks for the target user filtered by status (In Progress) and generation_started_at (recent window) to detect any live PAT work on the pod before takeover. Do NOT rely on the worker_id column (PAT claims don't stamp it).

OPEN QUESTIONS (all answered):
- Q1 driver location: reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/ (INSIDE reigh-worker repo, NOT reigh-worker-orchestrator). The driver imports SSH / runpod primitives FROM reigh-worker-orchestrator but lives in the worker repo.
- Q2 credentials: env vars RUNPOD_API_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN (never committed, loaded from .env or shell env).
- Q4 LTX model: resolve from reigh-worker source (travel_guidance.py / model registry) in Stage 1. Pick an actual supported LTX model name by reading the code, not guessing.
- Q5 individual_travel_segment standalone: existing handler already supports it as part of the travel flow. Use it directly — no synthetic parent needed.
- Q6 timeouts: longer to absorb model/asset downloads on fresh pods. Default travel_orchestrator 40 min, individual_travel_segment 25 min, image tasks 15 min. All configurable via flag.
- Q7 failure handling: run ALL tasks in the matrix regardless of individual failures. Emit one consolidated pass/fail report at the end showing per-task status, output URLs, durations, and error summaries.
- Q8 fixtures: pick good anchor images — 2 high-contrast scenes with clear subjects. Bake them into the driver as the default set, but make them swappable via config.

DEFAULTS (confirmed, not overridden):
- Flag 4 launch path: use run_worker.py via the supervisor (the canonical buildWorkerLaunchLine path from reigh-app/src/shared/components/SettingsModal/commandUtils.ts). Do NOT shell out to worker.py directly. Variant B worker restarts must kill BOTH supervisor.py AND its child worker process, then relaunch via run_worker.py.
- Flag 5 idle release: use --idle-release-minutes 0 which disables idle release (<=0 disables per source/runtime/worker/idle_release.py:41-43). Correct default.

VARIANT B TEARDOWN (B1/B2/B3):
- B1 pod restore: After the test finishes (pass or fail), restore the pod to its pre-takeover state — git checkout the original branch (captured at start of takeover) and relaunch the original supervisor+worker process. EXCEPTION: if the pre-takeover branch was itself a scratch/throwaway branch (e.g., another live-test/* branch or a detached HEAD), skip restoration and leave the worker stopped.
- B2 termination: Variant B defaults to --no-terminate TRUE. We do not own the pod, so never terminate by default; operator must explicitly opt in with a flag if they want termination.
- B3 Variant B sub-modes: Variant B supports TWO operating modes and must implement both:
  * B-existing: operator passes in an existing pod ID; driver assumes a Reigh-Worker install is already present at /workspace/Reigh-Worker.
  * B-fresh-takeover: driver spawns a fresh pod using create_pod_and_wait(), lets the standard production orchestrator startup template run (install + worker start), waits for the standard install to complete and the worker to come online, THEN performs the branch push + git pull + worker restart takeover. Same task matrix runs after takeover in both modes.

GLOBAL NOTES:
- Variant A folder name: use Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (or similar distinct name) at /workspace to avoid collision with any existing Reigh-Worker install.
- The plan must treat the individual-user PAT path as the PRIMARY worker auth mode for all test runs. Service role key is only present to unblock heartbeat writes and metadata updates, never for task claim calls.
- The driver is a single Python entrypoint with --variant fresh|update and mode flags, reusing SSH/pod primitives from reigh-worker-orchestrator.

  "meta_commentary": "Two execution-time tradeoffs from the gate are NOT in the plan body \u2014 they live only in the gate warnings and MUST be threaded into T14 (B-fresh-takeover). (1) spawn_worker() does NOT internally call start_worker_process(); the harness must call BOTH explicitly as two separate sequential steps. (2) worker_id and runpod_id are distinct UUIDs in the real orchestrator flow \u2014 generate a fresh worker_id, call create_worker_record(worker_id) FIRST, then spawn_worker(worker_id), capture the returned runpod_id, and thread them DISTINCTLY going forward (SSH/terminate use runpod_id; wait_until_ready and --worker flag use worker_id). The plan body's `wait_until_ready(db, pod_id)` and `--worker <pod_id>` are wrong for B-fresh-takeover; correct them when implementing T14.\n\nExecution order matters: land Phase 1-3 (T1-T12, Variant Fresh) FIRST. It is the cleanest path and does not touch the flagged subsystem. Variant Update B-existing (subset of T14) also works without the spawn_worker complexity. Variant Update B-fresh-takeover is the only mode requiring the accepted-tradeoff fixes.\n\nTests-first: T11 (unit tests) lands before any GPU code so failures surface in seconds, not minutes. The unit tests cover both process families and both safety-gate modes \u2014 no GPU minutes burned for primitive bugs.\n\nStage 1 (T1) is read-only and safety-critical. If T1 discovers schema drift, the production user_api_tokens still uses jti_hash, or spawn_worker is too tightly coupled to call from outside the orchestrator, STOP and consult the user before proceeding. Do not guess \u2014 verify.\n\nPhase 5 real GPU runs (Steps 22-23) are deliberately NOT in the task list as autonomous steps. T17 explicitly defers them to user authorization. Do not burn GPU minutes without an explicit go-ahead.\n\nDefaults: Variant Fresh terminates on success; Variant Update never terminates by default. Both honor REIGH_LIVE_TEST_NO_TERMINATE=1 env var.\n\nKey constraint reminders: (a) clone dir for Variant Fresh is /workspace/Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (not Reigh-Worker); (b) z_image_turbo task type has the _i2i suffix; (c) all four env vars must be exported into the pod (REIGH_ACCESS_TOKEN + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY + SUPABASE_URL + WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker); (d) push only to temp branch live-test/<ts>-<sha>, never main, never force; (e) test token loaded ONLY from REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN env, never hardcoded.",

        Idea:
Design a robust end-to-end live test harness for the Reigh platform that exercises the individual-user worker path (NOT the orchestrator-managed worker path) against a specific user identified by Reigh access [REDACTED] Two variants of one live test, both targeting a real RunPod GPU, both creating real spoof tasks in Supabase for that specific user, both waiting for actual task completion and verifying generations were produced end-to-end. Variant A 'Fresh Install': spin up a new RunPod pod using the orchestrator's create_pod_and_wait approach, SSH in and clone reigh-worker into a folder with a NEW name (NOT Reigh-Worker, e.g. Reigh-Worker-LiveTest), run buildWorkerLaunchLine-equivalent install/launch with [REDACTED] --wgp-profile 3 --idle-release-minutes 0, wait for heartbeat, insert spoof tasks in Supabase scoped to the user that the token resolves to (via user_api_tokens.jti_hash), poll until each task reaches Complete with generations row, report pass/fail per task with output URLs, terminate pod via terminate_pod() with opt-out flag. Variant B 'Update Existing': target an existing pod with /workspace/Reigh-Worker/ installed (or spawn+standard-install then take over), push current local working copy of reigh-worker/ to a temporary branch on banodoco/Reigh-Worker, SSH in, git fetch+checkout+pull, uv sync --locked, cleanly restart worker with --reigh-access-token for test user, run same task matrix, on success optionally delete temp branch and restore pod to previous branch/state. Variant B must not clobber pods doing real user work — include safety check for in-flight tasks. Task matrix (one of each): travel_orchestrator standard Wan 2 images 1 segment, travel_orchestrator LTX variant, individual_travel_segment single segment, qwen_image_style with style ref, qwen_image text-to-image, qwen_image_2512, qwen_image_edit, z_image_turbo I2I. Stages: (1) prep/finalize unknowns, (2) build shared primitives (token→user resolver, task spoofer, poll-until-complete, SSH helpers reused from orchestrator), (3) build Variant A driver, (4) build Variant B driver, (5) dry-run/smoke-test the harness itself, (6) first real run, (7) cleanup/documentation. For each stage: concrete deliverables, files to touch, risks, validation.

User notes and answers:
- User decisions on blockers and open questions (authoritative — supersedes earlier plan choices):

BLOCKER 1 (isolation): [REDACTED] is ALREADY a dedicated test user account. It has no production work and is explicitly a test token. User confirmed we can proceed using this token directly. Still do a defensive preflight check (abort if any unexpected non-test Queued/In-Progress task exists for the user, as a safety net), but no need to pause production, create a new test user, or use service-role for claims.

BLOCKER 2 (readiness signal): Option (a). Inject BOTH the PAT ([REDACTED]) AND SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY into the pod. The worker must still run the INDIVIDUAL-USER PAT path for task claims (WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker) — this is a hard requirement. The service role key is injected purely so heartbeat RPCs work and the standard ready_for_tasks detection path is available. Do NOT switch to service-role claim path.

BLOCKER 3 (Variant B takeover safety gate): Orchestrator's call — use option (a). Implement a PAT-aware in-flight check that queries tasks for the target user filtered by status (In Progress) and generation_started_at (recent window) to detect any live PAT work on the pod before takeover. Do NOT rely on the worker_id column (PAT claims don't stamp it).

OPEN QUESTIONS (all answered):
- Q1 driver location: reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/ (INSIDE reigh-worker repo, NOT reigh-worker-orchestrator). The driver imports SSH / runpod primitives FROM reigh-worker-orchestrator but lives in the worker repo.
- Q2 credentials: env vars RUNPOD_API_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN (never committed, loaded from .env or shell env).
- Q4 LTX model: resolve from reigh-worker source (travel_guidance.py / model registry) in Stage 1. Pick an actual supported LTX model name by reading the code, not guessing.
- Q5 individual_travel_segment standalone: existing handler already supports it as part of the travel flow. Use it directly — no synthetic parent needed.
- Q6 timeouts: longer to absorb model/asset downloads on fresh pods. Default travel_orchestrator 40 min, individual_travel_segment 25 min, image tasks 15 min. All configurable via flag.
- Q7 failure handling: run ALL tasks in the matrix regardless of individual failures. Emit one consolidated pass/fail report at the end showing per-task status, output URLs, durations, and error summaries.
- Q8 fixtures: pick good anchor images — 2 high-contrast scenes with clear subjects. Bake them into the driver as the default set, but make them swappable via config.

DEFAULTS (confirmed, not overridden):
- Flag 4 launch path: use run_worker.py via the supervisor (the canonical buildWorkerLaunchLine path from reigh-app/src/shared/components/SettingsModal/commandUtils.ts). Do NOT shell out to worker.py directly. Variant B worker restarts must kill BOTH supervisor.py AND its child worker process, then relaunch via run_worker.py.
- Flag 5 idle release: use --idle-release-minutes 0 which disables idle release (<=0 disables per source/runtime/worker/idle_release.py:41-43). Correct default.

VARIANT B TEARDOWN (B1/B2/B3):
- B1 pod restore: After the test finishes (pass or fail), restore the pod to its pre-takeover state — git checkout the original branch (captured at start of takeover) and relaunch the original supervisor+worker process. EXCEPTION: if the pre-takeover branch was itself a scratch/throwaway branch (e.g., another live-test/* branch or a detached HEAD), skip restoration and leave the worker stopped.
- B2 termination: Variant B defaults to --no-terminate TRUE. We do not own the pod, so never terminate by default; operator must explicitly opt in with a flag if they want termination.
- B3 Variant B sub-modes: Variant B supports TWO operating modes and must implement both:
  * B-existing: operator passes in an existing pod ID; driver assumes a Reigh-Worker install is already present at /workspace/Reigh-Worker.
  * B-fresh-takeover: driver spawns a fresh pod using create_pod_and_wait(), lets the standard production orchestrator startup template run (install + worker start), waits for the standard install to complete and the worker to come online, THEN performs the branch push + git pull + worker restart takeover. Same task matrix runs after takeover in both modes.

GLOBAL NOTES:
- Variant A folder name: use Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (or similar distinct name) at /workspace to avoid collision with any existing Reigh-Worker install.
- The plan must treat the individual-user PAT path as the PRIMARY worker auth mode for all test runs. Service role key is only present to unblock heartbeat writes and metadata updates, never for task claim calls.
- The driver is a single Python entrypoint with --variant fresh|update and mode flags, reusing SSH/pod primitives from reigh-worker-orchestrator.

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan's claim that `worker_state.py:200-204` (the 30-minute startup safety net) catches abandoned pods that exited before patching is slightly imprecise. line 200-204 only runs when `in_startup_phase` is true, which requires `startup_phase` to be in `('deps_installing', 'deps_verified', 'worker_starting')` per line 161. a pod that exits before its first patch has `startup_phase = none`, so `in_startup_phase` is false and the code falls through to the normal timeout checks (active_stale / not_claiming) at line 207+, not the 30-minute startup cap. both paths eventually reap the worker, so the end result is the same, but the overview's reasoning (naming 200-204 specifically) is wrong. worth correcting so future readers don't mis-reason about the invariant. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked worker_state.py line 161 (`in_startup_phase = startup_phase in (...)`) against the plan's assumption that subsequent lenient writes are safe. if deps_installing succeeds but deps_verified silently fails, startup_phase stays at 'deps_installing' and the 30-minute cap from line 200-204 applies — even though the pod is actually progressing through `uv sync`. on a slow runpod image with cold wheel downloads, `uv sync --extra cuda124` plus wan2gp deps can take 20+ minutes. there's no concrete benchmark in the plan that says the 30-minute cap is safely above the expected sync time; if `uv sync` legitimately takes 25 minutes and the deps_verified patch fails on a transient network blip, the orchestrator will terminate a healthy pod. plan should either bump the cap or note that deps_verified swallowing is acceptable because the cap is generously above typical sync time. > DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace

        Idea:
Design a robust end-to-end live test harness for the Reigh platform that exercises the individual-user worker path (NOT the orchestrator-managed worker path) against a specific user identified by Reigh access [REDACTED] Two variants of one live test, both targeting a real RunPod GPU, both creating real spoof tasks in Supabase for that specific user, both waiting for actual task completion and verifying generations were produced end-to-end. Variant A 'Fresh Install': spin up a new RunPod pod using the orchestrator's create_pod_and_wait approach, SSH in and clone reigh-worker into a folder with a NEW name (NOT Reigh-Worker, e.g. Reigh-Worker-LiveTest), run buildWorkerLaunchLine-equivalent install/launch with [REDACTED] --wgp-profile 3 --idle-release-minutes 0, wait for heartbeat, insert spoof tasks in Supabase scoped to the user that the token resolves to (via user_api_tokens.jti_hash), poll until each task reaches Complete with generations row, report pass/fail per task with output URLs, terminate pod via terminate_pod() with opt-out flag. Variant B 'Update Existing': target an existing pod with /workspace/Reigh-Worker/ installed (or spawn+standard-install then take over), push current local working copy of reigh-worker/ to a temporary branch on banodoco/Reigh-Worker, SSH in, git fetch+checkout+pull, uv sync --locked, cleanly restart worker with --reigh-access-token for test user, run same task matrix, on success optionally delete temp branch and restore pod to previous branch/state. Variant B must not clobber pods doing real user work — include safety check for in-flight tasks. Task matrix (one of each): travel_orchestrator standard Wan 2 images 1 segment, travel_orchestrator LTX variant, individual_travel_segment single segment, qwen_image_style with style ref, qwen_image text-to-image, qwen_image_2512, qwen_image_edit, z_image_turbo I2I. Stages: (1) prep/finalize unknowns, (2) build shared primitives (token→user resolver, task spoofer, poll-until-complete, SSH helpers reused from orchestrator), (3) build Variant A driver, (4) build Variant B driver, (5) dry-run/smoke-test the harness itself, (6) first real run, (7) cleanup/documentation. For each stage: concrete deliverables, files to touch, risks, validation.

User notes and answers:
- User decisions on blockers and open questions (authoritative — supersedes earlier plan choices):

BLOCKER 1 (isolation): [REDACTED] is ALREADY a dedicated test user account. It has no production work and is explicitly a test token. User confirmed we can proceed using this token directly. Still do a defensive preflight check (abort if any unexpected non-test Queued/In-Progress task exists for the user, as a safety net), but no need to pause production, create a new test user, or use service-role for claims.

BLOCKER 2 (readiness signal): Option (a). Inject BOTH the PAT ([REDACTED]) AND SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY into the pod. The worker must still run the INDIVIDUAL-USER PAT path for task claims (WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker) — this is a hard requirement. The service role key is injected purely so heartbeat RPCs work and the standard ready_for_tasks detection path is available. Do NOT switch to service-role claim path.

BLOCKER 3 (Variant B takeover safety gate): Orchestrator's call — use option (a). Implement a PAT-aware in-flight check that queries tasks for the target user filtered by status (In Progress) and generation_started_at (recent window) to detect any live PAT work on the pod before takeover. Do NOT rely on the worker_id column (PAT claims don't stamp it).

OPEN QUESTIONS (all answered):
- Q1 driver location: reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/ (INSIDE reigh-worker repo, NOT reigh-worker-orchestrator). The driver imports SSH / runpod primitives FROM reigh-worker-orchestrator but lives in the worker repo.
- Q2 credentials: env vars RUNPOD_API_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN (never committed, loaded from .env or shell env).
- Q4 LTX model: resolve from reigh-worker source (travel_guidance.py / model registry) in Stage 1. Pick an actual supported LTX model name by reading the code, not guessing.
- Q5 individual_travel_segment standalone: existing handler already supports it as part of the travel flow. Use it directly — no synthetic parent needed.
- Q6 timeouts: longer to absorb model/asset downloads on fresh pods. Default travel_orchestrator 40 min, individual_travel_segment 25 min, image tasks 15 min. All configurable via flag.
- Q7 failure handling: run ALL tasks in the matrix regardless of individual failures. Emit one consolidated pass/fail report at the end showing per-task status, output URLs, durations, and error summaries.
- Q8 fixtures: pick good anchor images — 2 high-contrast scenes with clear subjects. Bake them into the driver as the default set, but make them swappable via config.

DEFAULTS (confirmed, not overridden):
- Flag 4 launch path: use run_worker.py via the supervisor (the canonical buildWorkerLaunchLine path from reigh-app/src/shared/components/SettingsModal/commandUtils.ts). Do NOT shell out to worker.py directly. Variant B worker restarts must kill BOTH supervisor.py AND its child worker process, then relaunch via run_worker.py.
- Flag 5 idle release: use --idle-release-minutes 0 which disables idle release (<=0 disables per source/runtime/worker/idle_release.py:41-43). Correct default.

VARIANT B TEARDOWN (B1/B2/B3):
- B1 pod restore: After the test finishes (pass or fail), restore the pod to its pre-takeover state — git checkout the original branch (captured at start of takeover) and relaunch the original supervisor+worker process. EXCEPTION: if the pre-takeover branch was itself a scratch/throwaway branch (e.g., another live-test/* branch or a detached HEAD), skip restoration and leave the worker stopped.
- B2 termination: Variant B defaults to --no-terminate TRUE. We do not own the pod, so never terminate by default; operator must explicitly opt in with a flag if they want termination.
- B3 Variant B sub-modes: Variant B supports TWO operating modes and must implement both:
  * B-existing: operator passes in an existing pod ID; driver assumes a Reigh-Worker install is already present at /workspace/Reigh-Worker.
  * B-fresh-takeover: driver spawns a fresh pod using create_pod_and_wait(), lets the standard production orchestrator startup template run (install + worker start), waits for the standard install to complete and the worker to come online, THEN performs the branch push + git pull + worker restart takeover. Same task matrix runs after takeover in both modes.

GLOBAL NOTES:
- Variant A folder name: use Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (or similar distinct name) at /workspace to avoid collision with any existing Reigh-Worker install.
- The plan must treat the individual-user PAT path as the PRIMARY worker auth mode for all test runs. Service role key is only present to unblock heartbeat writes and metadata updates, never for task claim calls.
- The driver is a single Python entrypoint with --variant fresh|update and mode flags, reusing SSH/pod primitives from reigh-worker-orchestrator.

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked worker_state.py line 161 (`in_startup_phase = startup_phase in (...)`) against the plan's assumption that subsequent lenient writes are safe. if deps_installing succeeds but deps_verified silently fails, startup_phase stays at 'deps_installing' and the 30-minute cap from line 200-204 applies — even though the pod is actually progressing through `uv sync`. on a slow runpod image with cold wheel downloads, `uv sync --extra cuda124` plus wan2gp deps can take 20+ minutes. there's no concrete benchmark in the plan that says the 30-minute cap is safely above the expected sync time; if `uv sync` legitimately takes 25 minutes and the deps_verified patch fails on a transient network blip, the orchestrator will terminate a healthy pod. plan should either bump the cap or note that deps_verified swallowing is acceptable because the cap is generously above typical sync time.         Idea:
Design a robust end-to-end live test harness for the Reigh platform that exercises the individual-user worker path (NOT the orchestrator-managed worker path) against a specific user identified by Reigh access [REDACTED] Two variants of one live test, both targeting a real RunPod GPU, both creating real spoof tasks in Supabase for that specific user, both waiting for actual task completion and verifying generations were produced end-to-end. Variant A 'Fresh Install': spin up a new RunPod pod using the orchestrator's create_pod_and_wait approach, SSH in and clone reigh-worker into a folder with a NEW name (NOT Reigh-Worker, e.g. Reigh-Worker-LiveTest), run buildWorkerLaunchLine-equivalent install/launch with [REDACTED] --wgp-profile 3 --idle-release-minutes 0, wait for heartbeat, insert spoof tasks in Supabase scoped to the user that the token resolves to (via user_api_tokens.jti_hash), poll until each task reaches Complete with generations row, report pass/fail per task with output URLs, terminate pod via terminate_pod() with opt-out flag. Variant B 'Update Existing': target an existing pod with /workspace/Reigh-Worker/ installed (or spawn+standard-install then take over), push current local working copy of reigh-worker/ to a temporary branch on banodoco/Reigh-Worker, SSH in, git fetch+checkout+pull, uv sync --locked, cleanly restart worker with --reigh-access-token for test user, run same task matrix, on success optionally delete temp branch and restore pod to previous branch/state. Variant B must not clobber pods doing real user work — include safety check for in-flight tasks. Task matrix (one of each): travel_orchestrator standard Wan 2 images 1 segment, travel_orchestrator LTX variant, individual_travel_segment single segment, qwen_image_style with style ref, qwen_image text-to-image, qwen_image_2512, qwen_image_edit, z_image_turbo I2I. Stages: (1) prep/finalize unknowns, (2) build shared primitives (token→user resolver, task spoofer, poll-until-complete, SSH helpers reused from orchestrator), (3) build Variant A driver, (4) build Variant B driver, (5) dry-run/smoke-test the harness itself, (6) first real run, (7) cleanup/documentation. For each stage: concrete deliverables, files to touch, risks, validation.

User notes and answers:
- User decisions on blockers and open questions (authoritative — supersedes earlier plan choices):

BLOCKER 1 (isolation): [REDACTED] is ALREADY a dedicated test user account. It has no production work and is explicitly a test token. User confirmed we can proceed using this token directly. Still do a defensive preflight check (abort if any unexpected non-test Queued/In-Progress task exists for the user, as a safety net), but no need to pause production, create a new test user, or use service-role for claims.

BLOCKER 2 (readiness signal): Option (a). Inject BOTH the PAT ([REDACTED]) AND SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY into the pod. The worker must still run the INDIVIDUAL-USER PAT path for task claims (WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker) — this is a hard requirement. The service role key is injected purely so heartbeat RPCs work and the standard ready_for_tasks detection path is available. Do NOT switch to service-role claim path.

BLOCKER 3 (Variant B takeover safety gate): Orchestrator's call — use option (a). Implement a PAT-aware in-flight check that queries tasks for the target user filtered by status (In Progress) and generation_started_at (recent window) to detect any live PAT work on the pod before takeover. Do NOT rely on the worker_id column (PAT claims don't stamp it).

OPEN QUESTIONS (all answered):
- Q1 driver location: reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/ (INSIDE reigh-worker repo, NOT reigh-worker-orchestrator). The driver imports SSH / runpod primitives FROM reigh-worker-orchestrator but lives in the worker repo.
- Q2 credentials: env vars RUNPOD_API_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN (never committed, loaded from .env or shell env).
- Q4 LTX model: resolve from reigh-worker source (travel_guidance.py / model registry) in Stage 1. Pick an actual supported LTX model name by reading the code, not guessing.
- Q5 individual_travel_segment standalone: existing handler already supports it as part of the travel flow. Use it directly — no synthetic parent needed.
- Q6 timeouts: longer to absorb model/asset downloads on fresh pods. Default travel_orchestrator 40 min, individual_travel_segment 25 min, image tasks 15 min. All configurable via flag.
- Q7 failure handling: run ALL tasks in the matrix regardless of individual failures. Emit one consolidated pass/fail report at the end showing per-task status, output URLs, durations, and error summaries.
- Q8 fixtures: pick good anchor images — 2 high-contrast scenes with clear subjects. Bake them into the driver as the default set, but make them swappable via config.

DEFAULTS (confirmed, not overridden):
- Flag 4 launch path: use run_worker.py via the supervisor (the canonical buildWorkerLaunchLine path from reigh-app/src/shared/components/SettingsModal/commandUtils.ts). Do NOT shell out to worker.py directly. Variant B worker restarts must kill BOTH supervisor.py AND its child worker process, then relaunch via run_worker.py.
- Flag 5 idle release: use --idle-release-minutes 0 which disables idle release (<=0 disables per source/runtime/worker/idle_release.py:41-43). Correct default.

VARIANT B TEARDOWN (B1/B2/B3):
- B1 pod restore: After the test finishes (pass or fail), restore the pod to its pre-takeover state — git checkout the original branch (captured at start of takeover) and relaunch the original supervisor+worker process. EXCEPTION: if the pre-takeover branch was itself a scratch/throwaway branch (e.g., another live-test/* branch or a detached HEAD), skip restoration and leave the worker stopped.
- B2 termination: Variant B defaults to --no-terminate TRUE. We do not own the pod, so never terminate by default; operator must explicitly opt in with a flag if they want termination.
- B3 Variant B sub-modes: Variant B supports TWO operating modes and must implement both:
  * B-existing: operator passes in an existing pod ID; driver assumes a Reigh-Worker install is already present at /workspace/Reigh-Worker.
  * B-fresh-takeover: driver spawns a fresh pod using create_pod_and_wait(), lets the standard production orchestrator startup template run (install + worker start), waits for the standard install to complete and the worker to come online, THEN performs the branch push + git pull + worker restart takeover. Same task matrix runs after takeover in both modes.

GLOBAL NOTES:
- Variant A folder name: use Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (or similar distinct name) at /workspace to avoid collision with any existing Reigh-Worker install.
- The plan must treat the individual-user PAT path as the PRIMARY worker auth mode for all test runs. Service role key is only present to unblock heartbeat writes and metadata updates, never for task claim calls.
- The driver is a single Python entrypoint with --variant fresh|update and mode flags, reusing SSH/pod primitives from reigh-worker-orchestrator.

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked worker_state.py line 161 (`in_startup_phase = startup_phase in (...)`) against the plan's assumption that subsequent lenient writes are safe. if deps_installing succeeds but deps_verified silently fails, startup_phase stays at 'deps_installing' and the 30-minute cap from line 200-204 applies — even though the pod is actually progressing through `uv sync`. on a slow runpod image with cold wheel downloads, `uv sync --extra cuda124` plus wan2gp deps can take 20+ minutes. there's no concrete benchmark in the plan that says the 30-minute cap is safely above the expected sync time; if `uv sync` legitimately takes 25 minutes and the deps_verified patch fails on a transient network blip, the orchestrator will terminate a healthy pod. plan should either bump the cap or note that deps_verified swallowing is acceptable because the cap is generously above typical sync time.         Idea:
Design a robust end-to-end live test harness for the Reigh platform that exercises the individual-user worker path (NOT the orchestrator-managed worker path) against a specific user identified by Reigh access [REDACTED] Two variants of one live test, both targeting a real RunPod GPU, both creating real spoof tasks in Supabase for that specific user, both waiting for actual task completion and verifying generations were produced end-to-end. Variant A 'Fresh Install': spin up a new RunPod pod using the orchestrator's create_pod_and_wait approach, SSH in and clone reigh-worker into a folder with a NEW name (NOT Reigh-Worker, e.g. Reigh-Worker-LiveTest), run buildWorkerLaunchLine-equivalent install/launch with [REDACTED] --wgp-profile 3 --idle-release-minutes 0, wait for heartbeat, insert spoof tasks in Supabase scoped to the user that the token resolves to (via user_api_tokens.jti_hash), poll until each task reaches Complete with generations row, report pass/fail per task with output URLs, terminate pod via terminate_pod() with opt-out flag. Variant B 'Update Existing': target an existing pod with /workspace/Reigh-Worker/ installed (or spawn+standard-install then take over), push current local working copy of reigh-worker/ to a temporary branch on banodoco/Reigh-Worker, SSH in, git fetch+checkout+pull, uv sync --locked, cleanly restart worker with --reigh-access-token for test user, run same task matrix, on success optionally delete temp branch and restore pod to previous branch/state. Variant B must not clobber pods doing real user work — include safety check for in-flight tasks. Task matrix (one of each): travel_orchestrator standard Wan 2 images 1 segment, travel_orchestrator LTX variant, individual_travel_segment single segment, qwen_image_style with style ref, qwen_image text-to-image, qwen_image_2512, qwen_image_edit, z_image_turbo I2I. Stages: (1) prep/finalize unknowns, (2) build shared primitives (token→user resolver, task spoofer, poll-until-complete, SSH helpers reused from orchestrator), (3) build Variant A driver, (4) build Variant B driver, (5) dry-run/smoke-test the harness itself, (6) first real run, (7) cleanup/documentation. For each stage: concrete deliverables, files to touch, risks, validation.

User notes and answers:
- User decisions on blockers and open questions (authoritative — supersedes earlier plan choices):

BLOCKER 1 (isolation): [REDACTED] is ALREADY a dedicated test user account. It has no production work and is explicitly a test token. User confirmed we can proceed using this token directly. Still do a defensive preflight check (abort if any unexpected non-test Queued/In-Progress task exists for the user, as a safety net), but no need to pause production, create a new test user, or use service-role for claims.

BLOCKER 2 (readiness signal): Option (a). Inject BOTH the PAT ([REDACTED]) AND SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY into the pod. The worker must still run the INDIVIDUAL-USER PAT path for task claims (WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker) — this is a hard requirement. The service role key is injected purely so heartbeat RPCs work and the standard ready_for_tasks detection path is available. Do NOT switch to service-role claim path.

BLOCKER 3 (Variant B takeover safety gate): Orchestrator's call — use option (a). Implement a PAT-aware in-flight check that queries tasks for the target user filtered by status (In Progress) and generation_started_at (recent window) to detect any live PAT work on the pod before takeover. Do NOT rely on the worker_id column (PAT claims don't stamp it).

OPEN QUESTIONS (all answered):
- Q1 driver location: reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/ (INSIDE reigh-worker repo, NOT reigh-worker-orchestrator). The driver imports SSH / runpod primitives FROM reigh-worker-orchestrator but lives in the worker repo.
- Q2 credentials: env vars RUNPOD_API_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN (never committed, loaded from .env or shell env).
- Q4 LTX model: resolve from reigh-worker source (travel_guidance.py / model registry) in Stage 1. Pick an actual supported LTX model name by reading the code, not guessing.
- Q5 individual_travel_segment standalone: existing handler already supports it as part of the travel flow. Use it directly — no synthetic parent needed.
- Q6 timeouts: longer to absorb model/asset downloads on fresh pods. Default travel_orchestrator 40 min, individual_travel_segment 25 min, image tasks 15 min. All configurable via flag.
- Q7 failure handling: run ALL tasks in the matrix regardless of individual failures. Emit one consolidated pass/fail report at the end showing per-task status, output URLs, durations, and error summaries.
- Q8 fixtures: pick good anchor images — 2 high-contrast scenes with clear subjects. Bake them into the driver as the default set, but make them swappable via config.

DEFAULTS (confirmed, not overridden):
- Flag 4 launch path: use run_worker.py via the supervisor (the canonical buildWorkerLaunchLine path from reigh-app/src/shared/components/SettingsModal/commandUtils.ts). Do NOT shell out to worker.py directly. Variant B worker restarts must kill BOTH supervisor.py AND its child worker process, then relaunch via run_worker.py.
- Flag 5 idle release: use --idle-release-minutes 0 which disables idle release (<=0 disables per source/runtime/worker/idle_release.py:41-43). Correct default.

VARIANT B TEARDOWN (B1/B2/B3):
- B1 pod restore: After the test finishes (pass or fail), restore the pod to its pre-takeover state — git checkout the original branch (captured at start of takeover) and relaunch the original supervisor+worker process. EXCEPTION: if the pre-takeover branch was itself a scratch/throwaway branch (e.g., another live-test/* branch or a detached HEAD), skip restoration and leave the worker stopped.
- B2 termination: Variant B defaults to --no-terminate TRUE. We do not own the pod, so never terminate by default; operator must explicitly opt in with a flag if they want termination.
- B3 Variant B sub-modes: Variant B supports TWO operating modes and must implement both:
  * B-existing: operator passes in an existing pod ID; driver assumes a Reigh-Worker install is already present at /workspace/Reigh-Worker.
  * B-fresh-takeover: driver spawns a fresh pod using create_pod_and_wait(), lets the standard production orchestrator startup template run (install + worker start), waits for the standard install to complete and the worker to come online, THEN performs the branch push + git pull + worker restart takeover. Same task matrix runs after takeover in both modes.

GLOBAL NOTES:
- Variant A folder name: use Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (or similar distinct name) at /workspace to avoid collision with any existing Reigh-Worker install.
- The plan must treat the individual-user PAT path as the PRIMARY worker auth mode for all test runs. Service role key is only present to unblock heartbeat writes and metadata updates, never for task claim calls.
- The driver is a single Python entrypoint with --variant fresh|update and mode flags, reusing SSH/pod primitives from reigh-worker-orchestrator.

      "description": "Phase 4 Steps 19-20: create variant_update.py and main.py entrypoint. main.py CLI: `python -m scripts.live_test.main --variant {fresh,update} [--pod-id ID | --spawn-takeover] [--no-terminate | --terminate] [--dry-run] [--ref BRANCH] [--wgp-profile N] [--timeout-image 900 --timeout-travel-segment 1500 --timeout-travel-orchestrator 2400] [--anchor-image-a URL --anchor-image-b URL] [--serial]`. Defaults: fresh\u2192--terminate; update\u2192--no-terminate. Both honor REIGH_LIVE_TEST_NO_TERMINATE=1. variant_update.py supports two sub-modes: B-existing (--pod-id <id>) and B-fresh-takeover (--spawn-takeover).   "meta_commentary": "Two execution-time tradeoffs from the gate are NOT in the plan body \u2014 they live only in the gate warnings and MUST be threaded into T14 (B-fresh-takeover). (1) spawn_worker() does NOT internally call start_worker_process(); the harness must call BOTH explicitly as two separate sequential steps. (2) worker_id and runpod_id are distinct UUIDs in the real orchestrator flow \u2014 generate a fresh worker_id, call create_worker_record(worker_id) FIRST, then spawn_worker(worker_id), capture the returned runpod_id, and thread them DISTINCTLY going forward (SSH/terminate use runpod_id; wait_until_ready and --worker flag use worker_id). The plan body's `wait_until_ready(db, pod_id)` and `--worker <pod_id>` are wrong for B-fresh-takeover; correct them when implementing T14.\n\nExecution order matters: land Phase 1-3 (T1-T12, Variant Fresh) FIRST. It is the cleanest path and does not touch the flagged subsystem. Variant Update B-existing (subset of T14) also works without the spawn_worker complexity. Variant Update B-fresh-takeover is the only mode requiring the accepted-tradeoff fixes.\n\nTests-first: T11 (unit tests) lands before any GPU code so failures surface in seconds, not minutes. The unit tests cover both process families and both safety-gate modes \u2014 no GPU minutes burned for primitive bugs.\n\nStage 1 (T1) is read-only and safety-critical. If T1 discovers schema drift, the production user_api_tokens still uses jti_hash, or spawn_worker is too tightly coupled to call from outside the orchestrator, STOP and consult the user before proceeding. Do not guess \u2014 verify.\n\nPhase 5 real GPU runs (Steps 22-23) are deliberately NOT in the task list as autonomous steps. T17 explicitly defers them to user authorization. Do not burn GPU minutes without an explicit go-ahead.\n\nDefaults: Variant Fresh terminates on success; Variant Update never terminates by default. Both honor REIGH_LIVE_TEST_NO_TERMINATE=1 env var.\n\nKey constraint reminders: (a) clone dir for Variant Fresh is /workspace/Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (not Reigh-Worker); (b) z_image_turbo task type has the _i2i suffix; (c) all four env vars must be exported into the pod (REIGH_ACCESS_TOKEN + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY + SUPABASE_URL + WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker); (d) push only to temp branch live-test/<ts>-<sha>, never main, never force; (e) test token loaded ONLY from REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN env, never hardcoded.",

If a test fails and its ID appears in baseline_test_failures, it is pre-existing — do not scope-creep into fixing it. If baseline_test_failures is null, the baseline could not be captured; use your judgment but err on the side of assuming failures are regressions. You MUST still re-run the FULL test suite with your changes applied — pre-existing failures do not excuse skipping verification. Never narrow to individual test functions and stop.
        - If this batch includes the final verification task, write a short script that reproduces the exact bug described in the task, run it to confirm the fix resolves it, then delete the script.

        Idea:
Design a robust end-to-end live test harness for the Reigh platform that exercises the individual-user worker path (NOT the orchestrator-managed worker path) against a specific user identified by Reigh access [REDACTED] Two variants of one live test, both targeting a real RunPod GPU, both creating real spoof tasks in Supabase for that specific user, both waiting for actual task completion and verifying generations were produced end-to-end. Variant A 'Fresh Install': spin up a new RunPod pod using the orchestrator's create_pod_and_wait approach, SSH in and clone reigh-worker into a folder with a NEW name (NOT Reigh-Worker, e.g. Reigh-Worker-LiveTest), run buildWorkerLaunchLine-equivalent install/launch with [REDACTED] --wgp-profile 3 --idle-release-minutes 0, wait for heartbeat, insert spoof tasks in Supabase scoped to the user that the token resolves to (via user_api_tokens.jti_hash), poll until each task reaches Complete with generations row, report pass/fail per task with output URLs, terminate pod via terminate_pod() with opt-out flag. Variant B 'Update Existing': target an existing pod with /workspace/Reigh-Worker/ installed (or spawn+standard-install then take over), push current local working copy of reigh-worker/ to a temporary branch on banodoco/Reigh-Worker, SSH in, git fetch+checkout+pull, uv sync --locked, cleanly restart worker with --reigh-access-token for test user, run same task matrix, on success optionally delete temp branch and restore pod to previous branch/state. Variant B must not clobber pods doing real user work — include safety check for in-flight tasks. Task matrix (one of each): travel_orchestrator standard Wan 2 images 1 segment, travel_orchestrator LTX variant, individual_travel_segment single segment, qwen_image_style with style ref, qwen_image text-to-image, qwen_image_2512, qwen_image_edit, z_image_turbo I2I. Stages: (1) prep/finalize unknowns, (2) build shared primitives (token→user resolver, task spoofer, poll-until-complete, SSH helpers reused from orchestrator), (3) build Variant A driver, (4) build Variant B driver, (5) dry-run/smoke-test the harness itself, (6) first real run, (7) cleanup/documentation. For each stage: concrete deliverables, files to touch, risks, validation.

User notes and answers:
- User decisions on blockers and open questions (authoritative — supersedes earlier plan choices):

BLOCKER 1 (isolation): [REDACTED] is ALREADY a dedicated test user account. It has no production work and is explicitly a test token. User confirmed we can proceed using this token directly. Still do a defensive preflight check (abort if any unexpected non-test Queued/In-Progress task exists for the user, as a safety net), but no need to pause production, create a new test user, or use service-role for claims.

BLOCKER 2 (readiness signal): Option (a). Inject BOTH the PAT ([REDACTED]) AND SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY into the pod. The worker must still run the INDIVIDUAL-USER PAT path for task claims (WORKER_DB_CLIENT_AUTH_MODE=worker) — this is a hard requirement. The service role key is injected purely so heartbeat RPCs work and the standard ready_for_tasks detection path is available. Do NOT switch to service-role claim path.

BLOCKER 3 (Variant B takeover safety gate): Orchestrator's call — use option (a). Implement a PAT-aware in-flight check that queries tasks for the target user filtered by status (In Progress) and generation_started_at (recent window) to detect any live PAT work on the pod before takeover. Do NOT rely on the worker_id column (PAT claims don't stamp it).

OPEN QUESTIONS (all answered):
- Q1 driver location: reigh-worker/scripts/live_test/ (INSIDE reigh-worker repo, NOT reigh-worker-orchestrator). The driver imports SSH / runpod primitives FROM reigh-worker-orchestrator but lives in the worker repo.
- Q2 credentials: env vars RUNPOD_API_KEY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, REIGH_LIVE_TEST_TOKEN (never committed, loaded from .env or shell env).
- Q4 LTX model: resolve from reigh-worker source (travel_guidance.py / model registry) in Stage 1. Pick an actual supported LTX model name by reading the code, not guessing.
- Q5 individual_travel_segment standalone: existing handler already supports it as part of the travel flow. Use it directly — no synthetic parent needed.
- Q6 timeouts: longer to absorb model/asset downloads on fresh pods. Default travel_orchestrator 40 min, individual_travel_segment 25 min, image tasks 15 min. All configurable via flag.
- Q7 failure handling: run ALL tasks in the matrix regardless of individual failures. Emit one consolidated pass/fail report at the end showing per-task status, output URLs, durations, and error summaries.
- Q8 fixtures: pick good anchor images — 2 high-contrast scenes with clear subjects. Bake them into the driver as the default set, but make them swappable via config.

DEFAULTS (confirmed, not overridden):
- Flag 4 launch path: use run_worker.py via the supervisor (the canonical buildWorkerLaunchLine path from reigh-app/src/shared/components/SettingsModal/commandUtils.ts). Do NOT shell out to worker.py directly. Variant B worker restarts must kill BOTH supervisor.py AND its child worker process, then relaunch via run_worker.py.
- Flag 5 idle release: use --idle-release-minutes 0 which disables idle release (<=0 disables per source/runtime/worker/idle_release.py:41-43). Correct default.

VARIANT B TEARDOWN (B1/B2/B3):
- B1 pod restore: After the test finishes (pass or fail), restore the pod to its pre-takeover state — git checkout the original branch (captured at start of takeover) and relaunch the original supervisor+worker process. EXCEPTION: if the pre-takeover branch was itself a scratch/throwaway branch (e.g., another live-test/* branch or a detached HEAD), skip restoration and leave the worker stopped.
- B2 termination: Variant B defaults to --no-terminate TRUE. We do not own the pod, so never terminate by default; operator must explicitly opt in with a flag if they want termination.
- B3 Variant B sub-modes: Variant B supports TWO operating modes and must implement both:
  * B-existing: operator passes in an existing pod ID; driver assumes a Reigh-Worker install is already present at /workspace/Reigh-Worker.
  * B-fresh-takeover: driver spawns a fresh pod using create_pod_and_wait(), lets the standard production orchestrator startup template run (install + worker start), waits for the standard install to complete and the worker to come online, THEN performs the branch push + git pull + worker restart takeover. Same task matrix runs after takeover in both modes.

GLOBAL NOTES:
- Variant A folder name: use Reigh-Worker-LiveTest (or similar distinct name) at /workspace to avoid collision with any existing Reigh-Worker install.
- The plan must treat the individual-user PAT path as the PRIMARY worker auth mode for all test runs. Service role key is only present to unblock heartbeat writes and metadata updates, never for task claim calls.
- The driver is a single Python entrypoint with --variant fresh|update and mode flags, reusing SSH/pod primitives from reigh-worker-orchestrator.

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan's claim that `worker_state.py:200-204` (the 30-minute startup safety net) catches abandoned pods that exited before patching is slightly imprecise. line 200-204 only runs when `in_startup_phase` is true, which requires `startup_phase` to be in `('deps_installing', 'deps_verified', 'worker_starting')` per line 161. a pod that exits before its first patch has `startup_phase = none`, so `in_startup_phase` is false and the code falls through to the normal timeout checks (active_stale / not_claiming) at line 207+, not the 30-minute startup cap. both paths eventually reap the worker, so the end result is the same, but the overview's reasoning (naming 200-204 specifically) is wrong. worth correcting so future readers don't mis-reason about the invariant. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked worker_state.py line 161 (`in_startup_phase = startup_phase in (...)`) against the plan's assumption that subsequent lenient writes are safe. if deps_installing succeeds but deps_verified silently fails, startup_phase stays at 'deps_installing' and the 30-minute cap from line 200-204 applies — even though the pod is actually progressing through `uv sync`. on a slow runpod image with cold wheel downloads, `uv sync --extra cuda124` plus wan2gp deps can take 20+ minutes. there's no concrete benchmark in the plan that says the 30-minute cap is safely above the expected sync time; if `uv sync` legitimately takes 25 minutes and the deps_verified patch fails on a transient network blip, the orchestrator will terminate a healthy pod. plan should either bump the cap or note that deps_verified swallowing is acceptable because the cap is generously above typical sync time.
